svg.title: Wysiwys: current CRE confidential review architecture
svg.desc: The confidential handler delegates public chain reads to DON callbacks, verifies and decodes account data, evaluates private policy and sanctions screening, and exports only a bound report. Source agreement, CRE consensus and human votes are distinct. The runner confirms finalized guard state. Local simulation stops before report generation.
svg.text: Wysiwys: confidential review, guarded payout
Current frozen MVP | 117-byte report v2 | Solana devnet demo | 7 October 2026
App / Squads → Guard request_review → finalized event → listener / runner → CRE HTTP trigger
The trigger supplies multisig and transaction index only. Chain accounts supply authoritative payment facts.
Confidential handler: onReview
handlerInTee registration; live enclave or local simulation
1. Derive Guard / Squads account addresses
Public read requests cross through usingTheDons()
3. Verify, decode and evaluate inside the handler
Verify tx_hash; decode every stored instruction
Private policy: commitment, whitelist, mint, payment cap
Scorechain sanctions call with TeeRuntime secret
4. Release a minimal, bound verdict
Private policy and API credential stay in the handler
DON runtime: usingTheDons()
Public chain observations and derived report delivery
2. Node callbacks fetch finalized Solana state
Sources: QuickNode + Helius + Alchemy
Devnet health checks; shared floor and eligible sources
Application: two-of-three identical account contents
CRE: median slot floor, identical eligibility and account outputs
5. DON report → SolanaClient.writeReport
Require successful transaction and receiver execution
Require no error and a valid 64-byte signature
Only the derived bound payload crosses into report generation
agreed account data
destination follow-up uses the same read context
local-simulation exits here
Real reads and policy evaluation; no report generated or sent
diagnostic result only
6. Forwarder → Guard on_report → decided Review
Runner confirms finalized guard state before acknowledging
7. Human Squads votes AND approved, unexpired, unused Guard Review → guarded_execute
Recheck transaction and live destination → executor PDA signs Squads CPI → consume Review and pay atomically
Three distinct trust mechanisms
Provider agreement is application logic. Deployed DON consensus is CRE-managed. Human votes are Squads approvals.
Three providers do not configure DON membership or prove API truth. Local simulation does not prove real DON BFT or enclave attestation.
Devnet demo uses the simulator mock forwarder, which does not verify DON signatures. Live confidential execution requires separate access.
